title: Strawberry Ice Cream
subtitle: Custard-based ice cream with a whole fresh strawberry ripple
excerpt: A proper custard ice cream with fresh strawberry purée folded in during churning, so streaks of fruit stay visible in the finished scoop. Churn for 25 minutes, then freeze overnight.
sourceNotes: Custard-based strawberry ice cream has been made in Britain since at least the 18th century, when ice cream became fashionable in aristocratic households. The technique of folding in fruit purée during or after churning to create a ripple effect is a standard approach in British commercial and home ice cream making.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Press a sheet of baking paper against the surface before sealing to prevent ice crystals forming.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The custard base can be made a day ahead and kept covered in the fridge before churning.

content.text: Strawberry ice cream starts with an egg-yolk custard. Fold in fresh strawberry puree during the last few minutes of churning, so the fruit stays visible as streaks. The result is pale pink with a clean, sharp strawberry flavour rather than the sweetness of commercial versions.
Blend the hulled strawberries with 70g caster sugar and the lemon juice until smooth. Pass through a sieve to remove seeds. Transfer to the fridge to chill while you make the custard.

Whisk the egg yolks with 80g caster sugar in a large bowl until pale and slightly thickened. Combine the milk and cream in a medium saucepan and heat to just below boiling. Pour the hot cream mixture slowly onto the egg yolks, whisking constantly, then return to the saucepan over a low heat. Stir continuously with a wooden spoon for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens and coats the back of the spoon. Stir in the vanilla extract. Pour into a clean bowl, press cling film onto the surface, and cool completely. Transfer to the fridge for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Pour the cold custard into an ice cream maker and churn for about 20 minutes until thick and softly set. Add the chilled strawberry purée through the lid of the machine and churn for a further 3 to 5 minutes, the purée should ripple through rather than blend in completely. Transfer to a freezer-safe container, press baking paper against the surface, seal, and freeze for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until firm.

items.symptom: Ice cream is icy rather than creamy
items.cause: The custard was not chilled thoroughly before churning, or the machine bowl was not frozen sufficiently.
items.fix: Chill the custard for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Ensure the ice cream maker bowl has been in the freezer for the time specified by the manufacturer, typically 12 to 24 hours.

items.symptom: Strawberry ripple disappeared into the custard
items.cause: The purée was added too early, giving the machine time to blend it in fully.
items.fix: Add the purée in the last 3 minutes of churning, not at the beginning. For a more visible ripple, spoon the ice cream and purée in alternating layers into the container rather than adding the purée to the machine.

items.cause: The heat was too high, or the mixture was not stirred continuously.
items.fix: Keep the heat at low-medium and stir constantly without stopping. If the custard starts to look grainy, pour immediately through a fine sieve into a cold bowl, this can sometimes rescue a lightly curdled mixture.

content.text: Keeps in the freezer for up to 3 months. Remove from the freezer 5 minutes before scooping to allow it to soften slightly.
